title: Sales Development Rep
mission: Start enough good first conversations that the sales team always has qualified meetings to run.
outcomes_90_days: Reach a steady weekly count of outbound conversations that the team agrees on, with every prospect logged in the CRM.
Book qualified meetings at a rate the team can compare week to week, with a short written reason for each.
Keep a clean list: no duplicate contacts, every opt out honored the same day.
Hand over each meeting with notes the account executive can use without asking questions.

criteria.name: Outbound prospecting experience
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Has contacted strangers by email, phone or message on a regular schedule and can describe what they sent and what happened.
evidence_needed: Names the channels used and a typical weekly volume
Describes a reply rate or meeting count with how it was measured
Gives an example of a message they changed after poor results
levels: 0 no evidence of outbound prospecting
1 names outbound prospecting but gives no example
2 outbound prospecting done with guidance or at small scale
3 outbound prospecting done independently with a clear result
4 outbound prospecting with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows outbound prospecting with real examples

criteria.name: Clear short writing
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Writes a first message that is short, specific to the reader and easy to answer, with no filler.
evidence_needed: Writing sample or answer text is short and has one clear ask
Specific detail about the reader appears in the sample
No spelling errors that change meaning
levels: 0 no evidence of clear short writing
1 names clear short writing but gives no example
2 clear short writing done with guidance or at small scale
3 clear short writing done independently with a clear result
4 clear short writing with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows clear short writing with real examples

criteria.name: Follow up and persistence
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Keeps a system for follow ups and keeps going after silence or a no, while staying polite and respecting opt outs.
evidence_needed: Describes a follow up routine with timing
Gives an example of winning a reply after several touches
levels: 0 no evidence of follow up and persistence
1 names follow up and persistence but gives no example
2 follow up and persistence done with guidance or at small scale
3 follow up and persistence done independently with a clear result
4 follow up and persistence with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows follow up and persistence with real examples

criteria.name: Prospect research
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Spends a few minutes finding one true, relevant fact about a prospect before writing, never invents one.
evidence_needed: Describes where they look for facts
Example of a fact used and why it mattered
Mentions checking facts before using them
levels: 0 no evidence of prospect research
1 names prospect research but gives no example
2 prospect research done with guidance or at small scale
3 prospect research done independently with a clear result
4 prospect research with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows prospect research with real examples

criteria.name: CRM and tool habits

evidence_needed: Names a CRM or sheet used and what was logged
levels: 0 no evidence of CRM and tool habits

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?
Can the person work the hours the role needs, including any overlap with the prospects' time zone?

deal_breakers.description: Says they would keep contacting someone who asked to stop.
deal_breakers.job_related_reason: Outreach must respect opt outs to follow the law and protect the company name.

work_sample.title: Write a first message and a follow up
work_sample.brief: You get a one page description of our service and a fictional prospect profile (public facts only). Write one cold email and one follow up three days later. Then list in 5 lines how you would find and check 10 more prospects like this one.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score clear ask, one true specific detail from the profile, no invented facts, short length, a respectful follow up, and a realistic research method. Reply STOP line present counts as a plus.

interview_questions.question: Walk me through a normal week of outreach in your last role. How many people, which channels, what did you track?
good_answer_signs: Gives actual weekly numbers and channels
Names what they measured and what they changed
weak_answer_signs: Only says they did a lot of outreach

interview_questions.question: Tell me about a prospect who did not reply. What did you do over the next two weeks?
good_answer_signs: Stopped politely when it was clear

interview_questions.question: Here is a message that got no replies. What would you change and why?
good_answer_signs: Cuts length and sharpens one ask
weak_answer_signs: Adds more features to the text

red_flags: Cannot explain any numbers from past outreach
Talks only about volume, never about replies or meetings
Message samples with copied or invented personal details
Blames leads or the product for every miss
sourcing_channels: Local colleges and bootcamps with career offices
Former customer service or retail workers who like talking to people
pay_research_hint: Check recent postings for the same title in your city or region on two boards, and a published pay survey for your country. Compare base pay and the usual commission split. Use ranges, not one number.
automation_note: AI can find and draft first messages from public facts and sort replies, so a person focuses on the conversations. A tool should never send without a human approving the list and the text.
